column1: # An elided value or element is REFUSED (issue #48).
# It used to be a null, following the underlying jsonic. That made a
# mistake in the source indistinguishable from a deliberate `a:null` --
# a key whose value the author simply forgot to write generated happily
# as a null, and the document was wrong rather than rejected.

column4: written with no value after the colon

column1: # The error names the KEY or INDEX that was elided, not the container it
# sits in -- a document with many keys should not make the reader hunt.
# ... and what is NOT an elision. Each of these was a value all along and
# must stay one; refusing any of them would be a worse bug than the one
# An explicit null is a VALUE. This is the distinction the whole change
# exists to restore, so it is the first row.
# A colon chain is not an elision: `a:` is followed by the nested pair,
# A trailing comma is a separator, not an element.
# An empty map or list has nothing elided in it.
